# Sherpa UI — MCP server

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/check-mcp.mjs from the server's registrations. Do not edit it: npm run check:mcp -- --write -->

An MCP server for Sherpa UI, for an AI agent. It reads the `sherpa-ui` installed
beside it — its specs, schemas, docs and tokens — and runs its own checks, its
data layer and its usage check, never a copy of them. Each tool, resource and
prompt below is written from the code that registers it.

**20 tools · 10 resources · 3 prompts.**

## Setup

Node 22 or later. It is its own package, `sherpa-ui-mcp`, not on npm yet. An app
made by `npm create sherpa-ui` has it: its `.mcp.json` starts
`node node_modules/sherpa-ui-mcp/index.js`. In a sherpa-ui checkout, `npm run mcp`
runs it against the checkout. Any other client gives `node` and the full path:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "sherpa-ui": { "command": "node", "args": ["/full/path/to/sherpa-ui/mcp-server/index.js"] } } }
```

Do not use `npx sherpa-mcp`. On npm, `sherpa-mcp` is another author's package, and
a client with no terminal installs a missing one without asking.

## Tools

### The read tier's tools: what each component is, and the tokens · `tools/read.js`

#### `list_components` — List the components

Every sherpa-* component, by category: what it is, its slots and what each accepts, what it asks its provider for (`asks`), what it takes beside its data (`takes`) and the kinds it draws (`presents`). Start here; get_component gives one in full.

- `category` (optional) — Only this category, e.g. control, container, chart or data; `other` for a component with none

#### `get_component` — Get one component

One component in full: what it is, how to import it, its example as a page writes it, and its contract from its spec — its attributes, slots and what each accepts, what it asks its provider for, takes and presents, the settings it reads, its events, methods and properties. `include: "spec"` gives the whole spec as on disk.

- `name` — The element name, e.g. sherpa-data-grid
- `include` (optional) — contract (the default): what a page uses, with its example; spec: the whole spec as on disk

#### `find_token` — Find a token

The design tokens tokens.css declares whose names hold every word of the query: `surface`, `border accent`, `content/body`. A common word finds its token's word too: `bg` finds `surface`, `disabled` finds `inactive`. Each with its layer and its first value. An empty query lists the families.

- `query` — Words of a token name, e.g. surface, border accent or space; empty for the families

### The check tier's tools: an app, its markup and its data, checked · `tools/check.js`

#### `validate_page` — Validate a page

A Context's files, as text, checked by what sherpa-ui ships: its page definition against page.v1.json and then checkPage; its Views against views.v1.json, with each View's template read from `folder`; its template and each View's against the component specs (check_usage); and each `ui` — every id an element in the markup, every key a property or a method its spec lists. Give any of the three files. Each problem is said in its checker's own words. validate_app checks the files an app.json names, on disk.

- `definition` (optional) — The page definition, as JSON: the file a Context's `definition` names
- `views` (optional) — Its Views, as JSON: the file a Context's `views` names
- `template` (optional) — Its markup: the file a Context's `template` names
- `folder` (optional) — The folder the Views' file sits in, so a View's `template`, file.html#id, is read from it
- `own` (optional) — A project's own data-* hooks, by tag, as JSON, as its sherpa-usage.json "own" lists them: {"sherpa-button":["data-by"]}

#### `validate_app` — Validate an app

An app on disk, checked: its app.json against app.v1.json and then checkApp; that every file it names is in its folder; then each Context as validate_page checks it — its definition, its Views and their templates, its markup and each `ui` — and each Settings page's markup. The project's own data-* hooks come from its sherpa-usage.json. Run it after scaffold_app, and after every change to an app.

- `path` (optional) — The app.json, or the folder that holds it; relative paths start where the MCP runs. Default: the folder the MCP runs in
- `context` (optional) — Only this Context, by its name in app.json

#### `check_usage` — Check markup

Markup against the component specs, as `npx sherpa-ui check-usage` checks an app: every sherpa-* tag is a component, every data-* on one is its own or one every component may carry, an enum takes the value written, and a native button wearing `sherpa-button` takes the Button's names. A typo does nothing and says nothing in a browser; here it is a line.

- `markup` — The HTML: a template, a View's markup or a page
- `name` (optional) — What to call it in each line, e.g. its file: templates/records.html. Default: markup
- `own` (optional) — A project's own data-* hooks, by tag, as JSON, as its sherpa-usage.json "own" lists them: {"sherpa-button":["data-by"]}

#### `check_custom_node` — Check a Custom Node

A Custom Node's JSON, an entity (entity.v2) of the type node or any other type, checked as the shelf's Save checks it (plan 942 D3 A): against entity.v2.json, then `entityFaults`, over the app's other entities and its types. Each fault is said in words; with none, the node it offers: its use's kind, its category, its inputs and outputs, and how many nodes its graph holds. It writes nothing: an agent writes the JSON into the app's entities file itself

- `node` — The Custom Node, as JSON: `{ "v": 2, "type": "node", "id", "label", "graph": { "nodes", "connections" }, "settings": { "inputs", "outputs" } }`
- `entities` (optional) — The app's entities file, as JSON (entities.v3: `{ "v": 3, "types", "entities" }`, each type a type.v1 by its id), or a list of entities: its types are known, and a use of one of its entities is no fault

#### `describe_data` — Describe data

Rows, a JSON Schema or an OpenAPI document, or a page's own fields, said in Sherpa's terms: a TYPE (type.v1), which says each field's data once, with the evidence for each field; the controls a page keeps, where a page's fields were given; and the need a pattern is picked by (pattern.v1.json), which pick_pattern takes. The data layer makes the store's rules, what a page knows of each field and a grid's columns from the type. From rows nothing is drawn from a field's name, and nothing a sample cannot show is proposed; from a schema, what it promises may be said, and what no type field carries is listed. A status field is the type's, so the need counts one only when `status` gives it, and a child is the page's, so only when `fields` are given. Each output is checked against its contract before it is given. validate_rows checks the type against rows; generate_page takes it.

- `rows` (optional) — The rows, as a JSON array of plain objects: a real page of a real answer
- `schema` (optional) — Instead of rows: a JSON Schema of one row or of an array of rows, or an OpenAPI document, as JSON
- `fields` (optional) — Instead of rows: a page's own fields, as JSON — its definition's `source.fields` — split into its type's words and the controls the page keeps
- `status` (optional) — The status fields its store works out, as JSON (defs.v1.json statusField), each a field of the type: {"health":{"type":"status","values":[{"value":"At risk","status":"critical","when":[{"score":{"lt":60}}]},{"value":"Healthy"}]}}
- `id` (optional) — The type's id: what one row is, e.g. customer. Default: record
- `label` (optional) — The type's name, as a reader reads it. Default: from its id
- `path` (optional) — For an OpenAPI document: the path whose GET answers with the rows, e.g. /customers. Default: its first
- `key` (optional) — The field each row is known by. Default: id
- `task` (optional) — The agent's word for the work, for the need: browse, find, triage, edit, settings…
- `writes` (optional) — Whether a reader may change the rows, for the need

#### `validate_rows` — Validate rows

Rows against a type (type.v1), as sherpa-ui/data checks them: the rules its typeSchema() makes, each row run through its own validate(), and the rows read through a store made from the type (typeStoreOptions, with its status fields), which drops each row it refuses. Says how many pass, why each refused row was refused, and which fields the type does not name. The type is checked first: its schema, then typeFaults().

- `type` — The type, as JSON (type.v1), as describe_data gives it: { "v": 1, "id", "label", "fields": { "seats": { "type": "number", "min": 0 } } }
- `rows` — The rows, as a JSON array of plain objects

#### `scaffold_app` — Scaffold an app

A new app's files, as `npm create sherpa-ui <folder>` writes them: one folder with no build — index.html (the shell and outlet.start()), app.json, one Context's template, page definition and Views, its store with seed rows, its module, package.json, .mcp.json and an AGENTS.md that says where each kind of file goes. Write each into an empty folder, then `npm install && npm start`. Read sherpa://app-guide before changing them; validate_app checks them.

- `name` (optional) — The app's name: its package.json takes it, lower case with hyphens. Default: sherpa-app

### The query tier's tools: a page's Query run; any definition drawn as a graph and edited, through its lens · `tools/query.js`

#### `query_source` — Run a page's Query

Open a page as its provider does — `checkPage`, then `openSource` over the rows given, or over the app's data path on this machine — ask each command through `ask()`, and give what its components are given: the page of rows, the total before paging, the groups, each held field's state and its chip's results, the Query applied, and the data layer's own reports — every one, and each under the command that raised it; a command that moved neither the Query nor its page says `"changed": false`. A command is a `QueryRequest`, as a chip asks it: `{ "scope": "data", "field": "status", "reading": { "picked": ["active"] } }` (ticks); `{ "scope": "data", "field": "seats", "reading": { "tree": { "op": "gt", "value": 5 }, "mode": "advanced" } }` (a condition); `{ "field": "status", "reading": null }` (none); `{ "scope": "data", "sort": "seats", "direction": "desc" }`, `{ "group": "plan" }`, `{ "search": "acme" }`, `{ "page": 2 }`, `{ "scope": "data", "preset": "high-risk", "on": true }`, `{ "scope": "data", "suspended": true }` (its Switch), `{ "scope": "data", "hold": ["status"] }`, `{ "commit": true }` (Apply). Left out, `scope` is the View. The whole union is `QueryRequest` in sherpa-ui's src/core/data/query.ts.

- `definition` — The page definition (page.v1), as its JSON: `{ "v": 1, "id", "source": { "store", "fields", "scopes" } }`
- `rows` (optional) — The rows its store holds, as a JSON list. Left out with `data` left out, it has none
- `data` (optional) — In place of rows: the app's data path on this machine, e.g. `http://localhost:4200/` (its /sherpa/data/) or `http://localhost:4200/api/data/`; the store asked is the page's: its `source.store`, else its `type`. Any other host is refused
- `key` (optional) — With `rows`: the field each row is keyed by, e.g. id
- `type` (optional) — With `rows`: their type (type.v1), as describe_data gives it — the store is made from it, as the app makes it, so the page knows each field's words and status fields
- `commands` (optional) — Each a QueryRequest, asked in turn through `ask()`; a list inside one is one change
- `limit` (optional) — The most rows of the page to show; default 25

#### `definition_graph` — Draw a definition as a graph

A definition as the one Node Editor draws it, through its type's lens (`lensOf(type).toGraph`, plan 960 U4): a page's Query, opened over its rows as query_source opens it, or an entity, as its canvas edits it. Each node its kind's header, sockets and rows with their values, choices and `editable`, at its place; the connections; every fault its check reports; the graph as the definition the editor edits; and the kinds a graph may place

- `definition` — The definition: a page (page.v1), for its Query, as `{ "v": 1, "id", "source" }`; or an entity (entity.v2): a workflow, a Custom Node, a Filter, an app's own type
- `rows` (optional) — The rows its store holds, as a JSON list. Left out with `data` left out, it has none
- `data` (optional) — In place of rows: the app's data path on this machine, e.g. `http://localhost:4200/` (its /sherpa/data/) or `http://localhost:4200/api/data/`; the store asked is the page's: its `source.store`, else its `type`. Any other host is refused
- `key` (optional) — With `rows`: the field each row is keyed by, e.g. id
- `type` (optional) — With `rows`: their type (type.v1), as describe_data gives it — the store is made from it, as the app makes it, so the page knows each field's words and status fields
- `commands` (optional) — Each a QueryRequest, asked in turn through `ask()`; a list inside one is one change
- `of` (optional) — What the definition is: `query`, a page's Query; else an entity's type. Left out, it is read from the definition: a page has a `source`, an entity says its `type`
- `components` (optional) — For a page: the components it binds, each `{ "id", "label", "scope"?, "kind"? }`, so each scope reaches its own
- `fieldsOf` (optional) — Each store's fields, by the store's name — a page definition's `source.fields`, each with the `values` it may take: a Field row picks from those of the Source its rows come from
- `stores` (optional) — The stores a Source's Store row picks, by the names the app gives them
- `entities` (optional) — The app's entities file (entities.v3: `{ "v": 3, "types", "entities" }`, each type a type.v1 by its id) or a list of entities: each is a Custom Node a node may place by its use's kind, so a use of one is no fault (plan 942 D3 A)

#### `edit_definition_graph` — Edit a definition by its graph

Each edit made on the graph a definition's lens draws (`editWorkflow`, as the one Node Editor makes it): a row's value, `{ "node", "row", "value" }`; a node's own name, line or place, `{ "node", "set": { … } }`; a new connection, `{ "connection": { "from", "to" } }`. Then the graph is written back through the lens (`fromGraph`): the definition it says now, checked, or the faults that refuse it, in words. A page's Query asks each change as a chip asks it, and its page is saved as the Query holds it then (`pageWithQuery`)

- `definition` — The definition: a page (page.v1), for its Query, as `{ "v": 1, "id", "source" }`; or an entity (entity.v2): a workflow, a Custom Node, a Filter, an app's own type
- `rows` (optional) — The rows its store holds, as a JSON list. Left out with `data` left out, it has none
- `data` (optional) — In place of rows: the app's data path on this machine, e.g. `http://localhost:4200/` (its /sherpa/data/) or `http://localhost:4200/api/data/`; the store asked is the page's: its `source.store`, else its `type`. Any other host is refused
- `key` (optional) — With `rows`: the field each row is keyed by, e.g. id
- `type` (optional) — With `rows`: their type (type.v1), as describe_data gives it — the store is made from it, as the app makes it, so the page knows each field's words and status fields
- `commands` (optional) — Each a QueryRequest, asked in turn through `ask()`; a list inside one is one change
- `of` (optional) — What the definition is: `query`, a page's Query; else an entity's type. Left out, it is read from the definition: a page has a `source`, an entity says its `type`
- `components` (optional) — For a page: the components it binds, each `{ "id", "label", "scope"?, "kind"? }`, so each scope reaches its own
- `fieldsOf` (optional) — Each store's fields, by the store's name — a page definition's `source.fields`, each with the `values` it may take: a Field row picks from those of the Source its rows come from
- `stores` (optional) — The stores a Source's Store row picks, by the names the app gives them
- `entities` (optional) — The app's entities file (entities.v3: `{ "v": 3, "types", "entities" }`, each type a type.v1 by its id) or a list of entities: each is a Custom Node a node may place by its use's kind, so a use of one is no fault (plan 942 D3 A)
- `edits` — Each a WorkflowEdit, in turn

### The compose tier: a need → a pattern → a page, each page checked · `tools/compose.js`

#### `pick_pattern` — Pick a pattern

The patterns that fit a need, as describe_data gives it: each pattern's `when` run over the need as ONE row, through the data layer's own condition (`parseWhere`, `conditionClause`, `filterRows`). Highest `rank` first; each with every part of its `when` and whether it held, and the ones that do not fit, with the part that failed. Sherpa's patterns and the app's own — a patterns/ folder beside its app.json, where one of the same id replaces Sherpa's. A pattern that fits but fails checkPattern against the need is listed with its problems, never picked. generate_page makes the page from the first.

- `need` — The need, as JSON (pattern.v1.json need): `{ "task": "triage", "rows": 4200, "fields": 9, "dateFields": 1, "numberFields": 3, "statusFields": 1, "writes": true }`
- `app` (optional) — The app's folder, or its app.json, whose patterns/ folder adds the app's own patterns; relative paths start where the MCP runs. Default: the folder the MCP runs in

#### `generate_page` — Generate a page

A pattern and the data's type → a page: its template (the layout written as HTML, each `each` once per field of its kind), its page definition (the pattern's scopes with each `{kind}` the fields of that kind, its `ui`, and a grid's columns and key from the type; no field's words, which are the type's) and its first View; or, for a pattern with no data source, a Settings page's template. With the paths to write them at and the app.json entry; a page that draws its own View bar takes the header's away (`chrome.filters: false`). The pattern is checked against the need first (checkPattern), and every file by validate_page's own check before it is given: one that fails is refused, with what failed.

- `pattern` — A pattern's id, as pick_pattern gives it, or a pattern as JSON (pattern.v1.json), to try one of the app's own
- `id` — The page's id: its Context's name in app.json, and its files', e.g. customers
- `type` (optional) — The data's type, as JSON (type.v1), as describe_data gives it. Every page needs one
- `source` (optional) — The page's own part of its source, as JSON, as describe_data's "The page's own" gives it: what it searches and each field's control (select, advanced, op, child…), `{ "search": ["name"], "fields": { "customer": { "child": "site" } } }`. The words are the type's
- `store` (optional) — The name the app registers its store under. Default: the page's id
- `label` (optional) — Its row's name in the nav. Default: from its id
- `task` (optional) — The agent's word for the work, for the need, as pick_pattern was given it
- `writes` (optional) — Whether a reader may change the rows, for the need
- `app` (optional) — The app's folder, or its app.json, whose patterns/ folder adds the app's own patterns; relative paths start where the MCP runs. Default: the folder the MCP runs in

### The see tier's tools: a page drawn, acted on and read, and its acts traced · `tools/see.js`

#### `preview_page` — Preview a page

A Context drawn as a reader sees it: its page definition, template and Views served on this machine — at 127.0.0.1, on a port the system picks — by sherpa-ui's own Node host (`nodeHandler`), its data handler holding the sample rows as the store the page names, beside sherpa-ui's build; opened in a headless Chromium in the app shell a new app has, and waited for until the Context has loaded, its source answered and every component drawn (`settled`). Gives a screenshot, the data layer's own reports (`onReport` in the page), the usage problems (`check_usage` on the template and each View's markup), what the page threw and each request it was not answered, and its source's rows. The page asks nothing of another host and runs no inline script. One preview at a time: another closes it; preview_close ends it. Give an app's `path` and `context`, or the files. Its browser is Playwright's, `playwright-core`, a peer dependency npm installs beside this package: its Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium`), else the machine's Chrome.

- `path` (optional) — An app.json, or the folder that holds it, whose Context `context` is previewed: its three files read from disk. Relative paths start where the MCP runs
- `context` (optional) — With `path`: the Context, by its name in app.json. Default: its `default`
- `definition` (optional) — In place of `path`: the page definition (page.v1), as JSON — the file a Context's `definition` names
- `template` (optional) — In place of `path`: its markup — the file a Context's `template` names
- `views` (optional) — In place of `path`: its Views (views.v1), as JSON — the file a Context's `views` names
- `folder` (optional) — With the files: the folder the Views' file sits in, so each file a View names, file.html#id, is read from it and served
- `rows` (optional) — The rows the page's store holds, as a JSON list: a real page of a real answer. Default none
- `key` (optional) — The field each row is keyed by. Default: id
- `type` (optional) — The rows' type (type.v1), as describe_data gives it: the store is made from it, as the app makes it, so the page shows each field's words and status fields
- `view` (optional) — The View it opens on, by its id in the Views. Default: the first
- `width` (optional) — The window's width in px. Default 1280
- `height` (optional) — The window's height in px. Default 800
- `mode` (optional) — The display mode the page follows. Default light
- `own` (optional) — With the files: a project's own data-* hooks, by tag, as JSON, as its sherpa-usage.json "own" lists them. From `path`, its sherpa-usage.json is read

#### `call_component` — Call a component

Call a method a component's spec lists (get_component names them) on an element of the preview, or of a page on this machine, with JSON arguments; wait for the page — on the preview, until its source has answered and every component drawn — then give what it returned or threw, its attributes and any properties read back, and, on the preview, the data layer's reports during the act. watch_trace then says what the act did, by node. Only a Sherpa component's listed methods: no script crosses, and any host but this machine is refused.

- `selector` — A CSS selector for the element, `#grid` or `sherpa-pagination`: found in the page, else inside a component's shadow root
- `method` — The method to call: one its spec lists
- `args` (optional) — Its arguments, as a JSON list: `[2]`. Default none
- `readBack` (optional) — Properties to read after, as a JSON list of names: `["page"]`
- `url` (optional) — A page on this machine, `http://localhost:<port>/…`, in place of the preview; any other host is refused before anything opens
- `screenshot` (optional) — Give the page as it is after, as an image. Default false

#### `read_component` — Read a component

An element of the preview, or of a page on this machine, as it stands once drawn: its attributes; which states its spec names are on (each `states` selector tested on it); its properties — every one its spec says is readable, or those named; and the parts of its shadow root, each shown or not, with its text. It calls nothing. Any host but this machine is refused.

- `selector` — A CSS selector for the element, `#grid` or `sherpa-pagination`: found in the page, else inside a component's shadow root
- `props` (optional) — Properties to read, as a JSON list of names. Default: every property its spec says is readable
- `url` (optional) — A page on this machine, `http://localhost:<port>/…`, in place of the preview; any other host is refused before anything opens

#### `watch_trace` — Watch the trace

The spans of the last act, by the Query graph node each lights (`queryStepNode`) — node ids as definition_graph draws a page's Query: the MCP's own, each load of the last query_source, definition_graph or edit_definition_graph call; and the preview's, since it opened or since the last call_component — its page's and its Node host's, joined by their trace. Each step with its host, state, time and rows; what each load's walk counted is said under it (`traceQuerySteps`), each condition and preset with the rows it left.

- `node` (optional) — Only this node, by its id as definition_graph draws it: `when-data-status`, `source`, `store`

#### `preview_close` — Close the preview

End the preview: its pages, its browser and its Node host, so nothing of it listens or runs. Safe when none is open. preview_page closes the one before it too.

## Resources

### The read tier's resources: sherpa-ui's own files, as they ship · `resources/read.js`

| URI | Is |
|---|---|
| `sherpa://schemas/{name}` | **A contract.** A JSON Schema in sherpa-ui's schemas/, by name, at its newest version: `page` is page.v1.json, `workflow` workflow.v3.json. The contracts of an app's files, the shapes they share (`defs`), a component's spec and example, and a pattern |
| `sherpa://spec/{name}` | **A component's spec.** A component's `<name>.component.json`, as on disk: generated from its source and checked against the component schema |
| `sherpa://example/{name}` | **A component's example.** A component's `<name>.example.json`, as on disk: its markup as a page writes it, the data it is given, and when to use it |
| `sherpa://component/{name}/{kind}` | **A component's source.** A component's shipped .ts, .html or .css: its class, its template, its sheet |
| `sherpa://app-guide` | **Building an app on Sherpa.** How to build an app on Sherpa, step by step: the page, the shell, app.json, stores, a page definition, a template that asks, a Context module, Views, the session and starting the outlet (docs/APP-GUIDE.md) |
| `sherpa://data-rules` | **What Sherpa expects of your data.** The row shape, the conditions a query is made of, the Store contract, where validation belongs, and the data layer with no browser (docs/DATA-SOURCE-RULES.md) |
| `sherpa://tokens` | **The token sheet.** Every --sherpa-* token, by layer and mode, as the package ships it: src/styles/tokens/tokens.css, the source of `sherpa-ui/css` |

### The query tier's resources: the kinds every node graph is drawn from · `resources/query.js`

| URI | Is |
|---|---|
| `sherpa://node-kinds` | **The node kinds.** Every node kind sherpa-ui ships, as `NODE_KINDS` in `sherpa-ui/data` says it, by name: its heading, icon and description, its header's sockets (`input`, `output`), its rows (each `name`, `label`, `control` and sockets), the data layer's `model` for it, and the `graphs` it is drawn in — a page's Query, a workflow or both |

### The compose tier: a need → a pattern → a page, each page checked · `tools/compose.js`

| URI | Is |
|---|---|
| `sherpa://patterns` | **The patterns.** Every pattern pick_pattern picks from, as JSON: Sherpa's (sherpa-ui's patterns/) and the app's own (a patterns/ folder beside the app.json in the folder the MCP runs in), where one of the same id replaces Sherpa's — each one's id, label, use, when and rank, and where it is from; and each file refused, with why. Each is pattern.v1.json (`sherpa://schemas/pattern`) |
| `sherpa://pattern/{id}` | **A pattern.** One pattern, by id, as its file holds it: the app's where it has one of that id, else Sherpa's |

## Prompts

### The compose tier: a need → a pattern → a page, each page checked · `tools/compose.js`

- `build_page` — Build a page of a Sherpa app from its data: describe_data → pick_pattern → generate_page → validate_page → preview_page. The steps are skills/build-page/SKILL.md, the skill this package ships.
### The see tier's tools: a page drawn, acted on and read, and its acts traced · `tools/see.js`

- `review_page` — Review one Context: its files checked (validate_page), its markup against the specs (check_usage), then the page drawn over real rows (preview_page) — the data layer's reports, the usage problems and a screenshot — each problem fixed where it is named. The steps are skills/review-page/SKILL.md, the skill this package ships.
- `explain_page` — Explain how one Context's Query reaches its rows: drawn as nodes (definition_graph), one act a reader would make run (query_source), then the spans of that act by node (watch_trace) — each condition with the rows it left — said in the graph's terms. The steps are skills/explain-page/SKILL.md, the skill this package ships.

## Adding to it

A module registers its tools, resources or prompts and lists each in its header;
`MODULES` in `server.js` names the module. `npm run check:mcp -- --write` then
writes this file, and `npm run check:mcp` fails while it is stale.
